hotham.narrative: The temperature cooled overnight and it's a little crunchy underfoot this morning, but I expect it'll soften in many zones as the day warms.  The current temp is minus 1.2, heading for a top of 3 degrees. The wind is a light to moderate westerly, which is meant to ease further during the day. There's a little fog in the village right now, but the forecast is calling for it to clear up as the day progresses... so it should turn out pretty nice out there.  Heavenly Valley area is not perfect but there will be plenty of fun turns to be had for advanced and expert skiers and riders.  Just take notice of the signage, as some zones runs are upgraded, or may be closed if it's too slick. The Extreme Area remains closed due to a significant sliding hazard and please don't attempt to retrieve dropped equipment from closed areas. WRX First Tracks is scheduled for Road Runner from 7:30am.   It's pretty slick in the carparks, so take care while walking around this morning.     Cheers Bill.

hotham.narrative: It looks like a glorious day on the way.  The sky is full of stars and there is just a light breeze from the west, which is forecast to swing to the north and increase a little during the day.  The current temperature is just below zero and we are heading for a very pleasant top of 5 degrees.   The snow has had a decent freeze overnight, but it feels like there will be enough texture on the surface for firm but good turns on the groomers from the get-go.  Sunny aspects should soften for nice spring-like turns as the day warms but shaded and south facing slopes will likely stay pretty firm and slick for the day.  Follow the sun for fun turns all day.  Heavenly Valley area is not perfect but there will be plenty of fun turns to be had for advanced and expert skiers and riders.  Just take notice of the signage, as some zones runs are upgraded, or may be closed if it's too slick.   The Extreme Area remains closed due to a significant sliding hazard and please don't attempt to retrieve dropped equipment from any closed areas. Get out there and make the most of the great weather and fun snow conditions today, as it looks like we have some real mountain weather on the way tomorrow, and we should be waking up to a much whiter mountain on Wednesday morning.  Stay tuned! Cheers Bill.

Cheers Bill.

hotham.narrative: Thanks for letting me take this one Bill. The storm arrived, intensifying overnight and this morning we've woken up to 10cms on the stakes with the potential for more fresh cms to pile up before lifts open. Right now it's blowing and still snowing. I suspect the wind gauge has frozen up on the weather station but it's definitely strong from the West, which may ease later. The temp is currently -5.2 with the windchill making it feel much colder in exposed areas. It's a real mountain day. It'll be a morning for the storm riders. Keep an eye on upper lift status as I reckon some may be hampered by the strong winds, particularly early on. With the cold temps the snow has dried right out and will be great in the open areas. With wind transport, some areas will be deeper than others. Seek out the more sheltered zones for the best accumulation. While the overnight snowfall will have helped HV, be sure to take note of ropes and signage before launching in. Some areas have been upgraded in difficulty and are still thin with sharks lurking just beneath the surface waiting to catch out the over zealous. The Extreme Area remains closed so please stay out. There'll be heaps better turns to be found elsewhere anyway. Get out there and rip it up! Cheers, Burner.

Right now it's blowing and still snowing. I suspect the wind gauge has frozen up on the weather station but it's definitely strong from the West, which may ease later. The temp is currently -5.2 with the windchill making it feel much colder in exposed areas. It's a real mountain day. It'll be a morning for the storm riders. Keep an eye on upper lift status as I reckon some may be hampered by the strong winds, particularly early on. With the cold temps the snow has dried right out and will be great in the open areas. With wind transport, some areas will be deeper than others. Seek out the more sheltered zones for the best accumulation. While the overnight snowfall will have helped HV, be sure to take note of ropes and signage before launching in. Some areas have been upgraded in difficulty and are still thin with sharks lurking just beneath the surface waiting to catch out the over zealous. The Extreme Area remains closed so please stay out. There'll be heaps better turns to be found elsewhere anyway. Get out there and rip it up! Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: If you were out on the hill yesterday, I hope you had heaps of fun. It sure was nice to feel some soft dry snow underfoot. As forecast, snowfalls have eased. There's been a further 5cms recorded in the 24hr period with most of that falling during the day yesterday. At the moment there's just a very light fog in the Village but I can also see the moon and some stars. The current temp is a chilly -4.2 degrees and we're headed for a top of 1 degree. The wind has swung around to the South and is currently moderate at 30km/h which may ease further as the day progresses. With favourable conditions the guns have been going full noise all night and they're still blazing away as I type. With the combination of new snow, cold temps and snowmaking I reckon the open groomed terrain will be in tip top shape this morning perfect for laying your edges over. While the coverage on HV has improved, take care and observe all rope lines and signage. There are still many obstacles and some runs have been upgraded in difficulty. The Extreme Area remains closed so please stay away. Enjoy another day of great mid-winter like snow! Cheers, Burner.

Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: After a warm and very blustery night, the temperature has dropped and the wind has backed off a notch but is still a strong northerly.  The current temp is minus 1.5, heading for a top of 1 degree, there is high cloud in the sky, and we may see a snow shower or two during the day.  Due to the warm evening followed by rapid cooling in the last couple of hours, the snow is firm and slick out there this morning, but it should soften somewhat during the day.  It'll be a good morning for arcing turns on the groomers, but I'd avoid anything off-piste until there has been significant softening.  There'll hopefully be more significant softening with the top-up of snow expected over the next couple of days.  Stay tuned! Lifts are scheduled to open at 8.30 today but check the lift status before heading to your preferred option.  Sharpen those edges and feel the carve! Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: There has been a nice little refresh over the last couple of days. This morning we've got a further 7cms of new snow to add to yesterday's tally, bringing the total to 11cms so far from this system. At 6am it's still snowing lightly which is forecast to continue on and off throughout the day. The current temp is -2.5, headed for a top of -1 degrees and the wind is light to moderate from the NW. At the moment the snow feels reasonably dry underfoot and should make for some really fun turns with the best of it being had early before there's any temperature rise. The groomers will be in great shape from the outset, perfect for arcing some turns. Off piste is a little more tricky to read. I reckon some areas will have accumulated enough snow for some smooth turns, however, you might still be feeling the hard base underneath on ridge tops and some of the steeper terrain so be sure to feel it out before diving in. There are signs of significant promise beginning to show in the long range forecast and next week could be very interesting. Stay tuned to see how this develops over the coming days..... Have a great day out there! Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: I was surprised to see it snowing lightly walking across the carpark early this morning. While not a lot, it's added up to a fresh 2 centimetres and mixed in with some overnight snowmaking there should be some fun to be had out there today. The current temp is -1.9, headed for a top of 2 degrees and right now there's a moderate WNW wind with stronger gusts at times. There's still the odd fine flake in the air and a light fog in the Village. The texture on the groomers feels great underfoot and I reckon they'll be the best option first up on a very edgeable surface. With the cool temps off piste will likely be firm and probably best avoided until some softening occurs. For the early birds the Road Runner Quad will be spinning from 7:30am for WRX First Tracks. In more good news the Pirate Life Rail Jam is on tonight down at the Big D. Kicking off at 5:30pm, get along and check out all the action under lights! Rug up for the windchill and have a great day. Cheers, Burner.

hotham.narrative: It looks like a glorious day on the way.  The sky is clear, the snow guns are blazing and there is just a puff of a breeze from the north.  The overnight low was minus 5.8, the current temp is minus 4.8 and we are heading for a very pleasant top of 4 degrees.   The snow has firmed up a little since yesterday but the groomers I kicked on the way to the office have some nice dry texture on top.  It should be a good morning for carving turns on the piste, and some of the off-piste zones should be riding well too.  The sunny aspects should soften further as the day warms.   Get out there and make the most of the easy conditions today, as it looks like things are going to get real tomorrow. Stay tuned!  Road Runner will be spinning at 7.30am for First Tracks this morning.   And get along to support our incredible Volunteer Ski Patrol at the Big Gig fundraising auction tonight.  The General at 8.30pm.   Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: We have some weather coming folks.  Some high cloud has moved in, and the wind has picked up to a stiff northerly, which is meant to get increase significantly as the day progresses.  There is no precipitation at the moment, but there is a big blob moving our way on the radar. The current temp is minus 1, so hopefully the initial precip falls as snow and then we'll see what happens later on when the day warms.  Regardless, the temperature is forecast to plummet overnight, and heavy snow is predicted during the early hours, so we should wake to a much whiter mountain tomorrow morning. The snow has had a decent freeze overnight, so will start the day off firm before softening with precip of any type.   Get out there for the early turns.... or brave the elements when things get real later on.  Road Runner is scheduled for 7:30 First Tracks.    Cheers Bill

hotham.narrative: We have some weather coming folks.  Some high cloud has moved in, and the wind has picked up to a stiff northerly, which is meant to increase significantly as the day progresses.  There is no precipitation at the moment, but there is a big blob moving our way on the radar. The current temp is minus 1, so hopefully the initial precip falls as snow and then we'll see what happens later on when the day warms.  Regardless, the temperature is forecast to plummet overnight, and heavy snow is predicted during the early hours, so we should wake to a much whiter mountain tomorrow morning. The snow has had a decent freeze overnight, so will start the day off firm before softening with precip of any type. Get out there for the early turns.... or brave the elements when things get real later on.  Road Runner is scheduled for 7:30am First Tracks.    Cheers Bill

perisher.narrative: Mostly sunny Sunday at Perisher. Sunday's shaping up mostly sunny, with a top of 6 degrees and light westerly winds around 16km/h. 29 lifts are expected to spin today, but as always, keep an eye on the lift report for real-time updates, or download the Perisher App to stay in the loop. With 34 groomed runs across the resort, expect firm, fast conditions and hard-packed snow underfoot. Leichhardt Park officially opened yesterday for the first time this winter, so grab your mates and get amongst it for some park laps. If you're keen to try before you buy, today's your last chance to demo the latest gear from Faction and Dynastar. Head to the Mt Perisher Powder Inn between 9am and 3pm to say hello and put it through its paces. The good times continue off the slopes too, with live music around the mountain all day: Will Clift at Jax Bar, Matty Rogers at Blue Cow, and DJ Bolta bringing the beats at the Red Bull Boom Box. Have a great Sunday!

perisher.narrative: Bluebird to start the week. The bluebird weather continues, with another sunny day on the cards for Monday. We're expecting to see a top of 8 degrees and light north-westerly around 15km/h. Last night, the temperatures dipped to -4 degrees, giving the snowmaking team an opportunity to fire up the guns. We had 145 guns running across the resort from 8:00pm and still going at time of writing! Conditions on the slopes will be firm and fast underfoot, with hard-packed snow topped with a layer of man-made. We have 29 lifts scheduled to spin today, and 35 groomed runs for you to enjoy some sunny laps. As always, please keep an eye on the lift report for real-time updates, or download the Perisher App to stay in the loop. Enjoy the sunshine!

perisher.narrative: Another 7cm, snowmaking and clear skies!. We had another 7cm throughout the day yesterday and into last night, bringing the storm total to 15cm. With wind-blown pockets, you can definitely find some deeper stashes out there. The temperature remained cold, so we've also had a really solid run of snowmaking with the guns still running this morning and adding to the coverage. It's currently -4.7 degrees in Perisher Valley and we're headed for a top of 2 degrees. The wind is around 15km/h from the south-west and it's forecast to stay that way for most of the day. The sky is clear, and with 37 groomed runs across the resort, 30 lifts expected to open and a cold, dry snow surface, plus plenty of powder stashes, this could be the day of the season so far! Blue Calf T-Bar will come back online to give people in Guthega an option for skiing and riding, giving us four resort areas open once again! Around the resort, there's live music at Jax and in Blue Cow this afternoon. Check the Events page or follow Perisher's socials to stay across all the action. Head out there and have a great day!

perisher.narrative: More sunshine and snowmaking!. We're kicking off the weekend with a bluebird day at Perisher! Expect sun and a top of 6 degrees, with north-westerly winds 15 to 20 km/h becoming light in the early afternoon. It was a chilly night in-resort last night - the temp dipped to -9 degrees and it's currently only -8 degrees, making for a great night of snowmaking. We had 172 guns firing from 6:30pm and still going at time of writing, helping to top up the base with man-made snow off the back of our last snowfall. Please note, the best skiing and riding remain in the snowmaking areas , and coverage may be thin elsewhere. The most recent snowfall allowed us to open up some more lifts and terrain. 36 lifts are scheduled to spin today, and the team are working hard behind the scenes to get more open as quickly as possible. Be sure to keep an eye on the lift report for real-time updates or download the Perisher App to stay in the loop. There will be 48 groomed runs for you to enjoy some sunny laps. Around the resort today, Chicks Who Shred will be ripping around, and there's plenty of live music; Valley Animal Duo at Blue Cow, Will Clift at Jax Bar, and DJ Bolta at Mid-Station! Night Skiing and Boarding is also taking place after-dark on Front Valley, with a special fireworks show at 7:00pm. The vibes are high with more snow in the forecast.... but for now, enjoy the sunshine!

perisher.narrative: Another 10cm of fresh snow! . It was snowing heavily as the resort closed yesterday and we had another 10cm of snow overnight , bringing the total for the week to 18cm. Winter might have been a little late this year, but it's well and truly arrived with the start of August. It's currently a chilly -3 degrees in Perisher Valley and the wind is blowing from the southwest at around 15-20km/h. We're headed for a top of 3 degrees. This morning's fog is lifting as I write this and the forecast is calling for a partly cloudy day, so it should clear up and visibility will be fine. There isn't any more snow forecast today and we should be in for a couple of clear days before the next front rolls in. Speaking of the next front, that looks to be the big one, with the Weatherzone forecast calling for between 47cm and 95cm of snow from Sunday through to Thursday next week. The snow guns were also firing overnight to add to the natural snowfall. We have 38 lifts scheduled to run and 55 groomed runs across the resort, and the skiing and riding will be awesome. With the fresh snow, we may have additional lifts come online over the coming days, so download the Perisher App to be the first to know, and keep an eye on the lift report for real-time updates. It will be a great day out there, so get out and enjoy it!

perisher.narrative: Three resort areas interlinked!. Happy Friday and good morning from Perisher! We have some high cloud about this morning and the chance of a snow flurry, but the forecast is calling for a mostly sunny day. Conditions are expected to clear as the day wears on. It's currently -1 degrees in Perisher Valley with a forecast top of 4 degrees. The wind is blowing from the west at around 20km/h and should stay that way for most of the day. 178 snow guns ran from 4:30pm yesterday until about midnight, when the relative humidity rose. The great news is we have 41 lifts scheduled to run today, with Interceptor opening yesterday and Sun Valley and Freedom Quad scheduled for today. Plus, three resort areas connected , with skiing between Perisher Valley, Blue Cow and Guthega now on offer. You can ski from Perisher to Smiggins via Piper T-Bar, but you'll need to take the free Guest Shuttle to return to Perisher Valley. With 62 runs groomed across the resort, it's going to be a great day out there, with plenty of room to explore. The groomers will be fast and off-piste will be variable, check it out before going all in! In events, the Blue Cow Cup kicks off today, now relocated to Perisher, with racing on Front Valley. Plus check out live entertainment at Mid Station, Blue Cow and Jax during the day. Have a great day out there!

perisher.narrative: Wild winter weather ahead. Perisher is set for some wild winter weather today! It's currently 1 degrees, and while this morning brings a mix of sun and cloud, conditions will turn as the day progresses, with high cloud and wind moving in. We suggest making the most of the morning! Blizzard-like conditions are due to roll in this afternoon, bringing rain that should hopefully fall as snow at the peaks. Today's top will be 4 degrees, with north-westerly winds of 30 to 45 km/h and stronger gusts here and there. High wind may impact lift operations, so check the lift report for real-time updates, or download the Perisher App to stay in the loop! 41 lifts scheduled to spin today and 64 groomed runs to carve up. Conditions on the slopes will be hard packed with some man-made snow on top, as the snow guns have been running since around 9pm last night and are still going this morning. With cloud cover rolling in, visibility on the slopes could be affected, so please take care while skiing and boarding. In between runs, catch some live music from the Greg Nunan Duo at Jax Bar and the Steve Edmonds Band at Blue Cow Bistro! We should start reaping the benefits of this storm tomorrow, with rain turning to snow showers overnight and continuing through the day! The days following are also looking promising for snowfall , so stay tuned to see how much we get.

latest.narrative: Wild winter weather ahead. Perisher is set for some wild winter weather today! It's currently 1 degrees, and while this morning brings a mix of sun and cloud, conditions will turn as the day progresses, with high cloud and wind moving in. We suggest making the most of the morning! Blizzard-like conditions are due to roll in this afternoon, bringing rain that should hopefully fall as snow at the peaks. Today's top will be 4 degrees, with north-westerly winds of 30 to 45 km/h and stronger gusts here and there. High wind may impact lift operations, so check the lift report for real-time updates, or download the Perisher App to stay in the loop! 41 lifts scheduled to spin today and 64 groomed runs to carve up. Conditions on the slopes will be hard packed with some man-made snow on top, as the snow guns have been running since around 9pm last night and are still going this morning. With cloud cover rolling in, visibility on the slopes could be affected, so please take care while skiing and boarding. In between runs, catch some live music from the Greg Nunan Duo at Jax Bar and the Steve Edmonds Band at Blue Cow Bistro! We should start reaping the benefits of this storm tomorrow, with rain turning to snow showers overnight and continuing through the day! The days following are also looking promising for snowfall , so stay tuned to see how much we get.

latest.narrative: We have some weather coming folks.  Some high cloud has moved in, and the wind has picked up to a stiff northerly, which is meant to increase significantly as the day progresses.  There is no precipitation at the moment, but there is a big blob moving our way on the radar. The current temp is minus 1, so hopefully the initial precip falls as snow and then we'll see what happens later on when the day warms.  Regardless, the temperature is forecast to plummet overnight, and heavy snow is predicted during the early hours, so we should wake to a much whiter mountain tomorrow morning. The snow has had a decent freeze overnight, so will start the day off firm before softening with precip of any type. Get out there for the early turns.... or brave the elements when things get real later on.  Road Runner is scheduled for 7:30am First Tracks.    Cheers Bill

August is a big month on the mountain, with a packed calendar of on-snow events, races and activities, alongside plenty to enjoy off the slopes. From exciting action on the snow and Nordic trails to live music, food, family activities and events across the village, there’s something happening throughout the month.
